This happens occasionally due to intensive bowel surgery many years ago. Paramedics inject morphine and as it’s a controlled drug he’s taken into hospital overnight to be monitored. Around 3.30am I rang 999 for assistance. Paramedics arrived and asked if he’d try a paracetamol drip as this didn’t require hospital monitoring. He agreed and within 10 minutes the pain subsided. They did advise him to go to the hospital but said if he decided not to, ring the doctors in the morning for a face to face appointment to be checked over. At 8am I rang surgery and explained the situation only to be met with “Well if he wouldn’t go to the hospital what do you want a GP to do? I explained I was following instructions given to me. Frankly I found Sharon’s attitude abysmal and asked her not to talk down to me. She said a doctor would call back. Half an hour later I had a call from the surgery from someone sounding far less aggressive saying they had gone over my husband’s notes and noticed that the paramedics had booked him an appointment for 9.30am. Obviously Sharon hadn’t responded to them as she had to me! When you’ve been up all night trying to support someone in intense pain this is the last thing you need - especially in your 80th year!
May I add that we’ve never had any issues with the doctors who have always gone out of their way to help, it’s solely a reception problem.",null,[0,238]]]],[],[null,null,null,["https://www.google.com/maps/reviews/data=!4m8!14m7!1m6!2m5!1sChZDSUhNMG9nS0VJQ0FnTURJdG9qMU5REAE!2m1!1s0x0:0x38e3cb20663d722a!3m1!1s2@1:CIHM0ogKEICAgMDItoj1NQ%7C%7C?hl=en"],["https://www.google.com/local/content/rap/report?postId=ChZDSUhNMG9nS0VJQ0FnTURJdG9qMU5REAE&t=1&entityid=ChZDSUhNMG9nS0VJQ0FnTURJdG9qMU5REi4KF0NJSE0wb2dLRUlDQWdNREl0b2oxdFFFEhNDZ3dJdkxEYnZ3WVFxS1RpNndFGiwKFkNJSE0wb2dLRUlDQWdNREl0b2oxZFESEkNnc0lsYUxhdndZUWdOLTNiZyISCQAAAAAAAAAAESpyPWYgy-M4KhNDZ3dJdkxEYnZ3WVFxS1RpNndF&wv=1&d=286732320",null,null,"0ahUKEwj6-ofavrOTAxWSdIQGHRKjEpQQoykICigB"],null,[null,[[1,0]]]],"0ahUKEwj6-ofavrOTAxWSdIQGHRKjEpQQ0pMFCAgoAg"],null,"CAESY0NBRVFBeHBFUTJwRlNVRlNTWEJEWjI5QlVEZGZURU5EYjBSZlgxOWZSV2hCWTJwZmJ6WjVkRUphUmpWZlZYVnFhMEZCUVVGQlIyZHVPVEpwTkVOaFpWQkVWVGRGV1VGRFNVRQ=="],[["ChdDSUhNMG9nS0VJQ0FnSUQzczZlNndnRRAB",["0x0:0x38e3cb20663d722a",null,1731954247167417,1731954247167417,[null,null,["https://www.google.com/maps/contrib/105327221405758487449/reviews?hl=en"],null,null,["Anthony Chisman","https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/a/ACg8ocKCXn2VO5dIcI8fkk6jerz3xDcHhkYvqbxLcoFA90luQ694HQ=s120-c-rp-mo-br100",["https://www.google.com/maps/contrib/105327221405758487449?hl=en"],"105327221405758487449",null,6,3,null,[0,3,1],0,["6 reviews",null,null,null,null,[null,"0ahUKEwj6-ofavrOTAxWSdIQGHRKjEpQQ7LoGCAwoAA"]]]],null,"a year ago",null,null,null,null,null,null,["Google","https://www.gstatic.com/images/branding/product/1x/googleg_48dp.png",null,null,5],null,1],[[2],null,null,null,null,null,null,null,null,null,null,null,null,null,["en"],[["The first doctors surgery I've ever come across that is stuck in the 1980's. As of April 2024, my experiences with the surgery has seemingly improved a lot. it's easier to communicate with the front desk, who are now more politer in their manner of speaking. Sometimes they take an abrupt straight up approach when explaining something but at least they're honest.

The GP's are still fantastic and friendly and understanding and the surgery just seems less hostile than it used to be.

There are still some things that can be improved on, it's still hard to get an appointment when calling on the day, however since signing up with the nhs app, I can book appointments on the app and this saves having to ring every day to see if there's one available.

Although improved, it does still look like the surgery, like most others, struggles to keep up with increased demand, and this can sometimes delay things, and reduce the communication efforts that they have with other services but that's not their fault and overall I appreciate the effort everyone working there puts in and appreciate the improved bedside manner.

My best friend soul mate and the love of my life.
I have been taking small doses of diazapam and was actually going into to get a repeat prescription and to ask about lowering the dose and hopefully going on not needing it.
I was met a total blank of your not having anymore and something like a bad comedy sketch of look on the bright side of life that I'm some kind of drug addict.
I said I had been waiting and asking for help for over 2 months now and got absolutely nothing in the way of any response. The reply o its better now it used to be a year , with a smile. I said my wife was my soul mate and the response "well that's something then isn't it".
I read my notes on my NHS app saying I'd discussed and the way forward wasn't drugs and counselling was the answer ( which there isn't any) . I'd agree but I think a first year med school grad would think twice from taking someone on 2 months of diazapam from the loss of his soul mate ,to absolutely nothing when they come into a surgery with obvious serious anxiety and depression.
I actually walked out on him I was so disgusted.
The surgery helped my wife alot.and the support I have recieved from other Dr's, the support team and reception have been fantastic.
I'm sorry to have to write this but after telling my friends after having one of the worst 4 days of my life copeing on my own and not sure I'd be here today if it hadn't been for them they Said to actually complain.
I'm not writing this in spite of not getting what I want .Just the total lack of empathy, respect for someone grieving, was an absolute disgrace.
I think he needs taking out and retraining in grief and empathy.
I've been given a contact of support group now so fingers crossed.
I'm asking for this Dr to never ever see me again or make any decisions on any future repeat prescription for me.
Thanks to the rest of you there
Alan Hawley",null,[0,158]]]],[],[null,null,null,["https://www.google.com/maps/reviews/data=!4m8!14m7!1m6!2m5!1sChdDSUhNMG9nS0VJQ0FnSURudVlqYzJBRRAB!2m1!1s0x0:0x38e3cb20663d722a!3m1!1s2@1:CIHM0ogKEICAgIDnuYjc2AE%7C%7C?hl=en"],["https://www.google.com/local/content/rap/report?postId=ChdDSUhNMG9nS0VJQ0FnSURudVlqYzJBRRAB&t=1&entityid=ChdDSUhNMG9nS0VJQ0FnSURudVlqYzJBRRItChZDSUhNMG9nS0VJQ0FnSURudVlqY09BEhNDZ3dJLTRHUXVBWVFrTXY5cEFJGi4KF0NJSE0wb2dLRUlDQWdJRG51WWpjdUFFEhNDZ3dJLTRHUXVBWVFrTXY5cEFJIhIJAAAAAAAAAAARKnI9ZiDL4zgqE0Nnd0ktNEdRdUFZUWtNdjlwQUk&wv=1&d=286732320",null,null,"0ahUKEwj6-ofavrOTAxWSdIQGHRKjEpQQoykIEygB"],null,[null,[[1,0]]]],"0ahUKEwj6-ofavrOTAxWSdIQGHRKjEpQQ0pMFCBEoBQ"],null,"CAESY0NBRVFCaHBFUTJwRlNVRlNTWEJEWjI5QlVEZGZURVI2VFU5ZlgxOWZSV2hCYTJ3M2VGWnZOWEpRT0ZGMFIwVkJRVUZCUVVGQlIyZHVPVEl3UlVOaVdtaGpTMU5GV1VGRFNVRQ=="],[["ChZDSUhNMG9nS0VJQ0FnSURIdF9PaFN3EAE",["0x0:0x38e3cb20663d722a",null,1726868461287246,1726868461287246,[null,null,["https://www.google.com/maps/contrib/113996470762991177946/reviews?hl=en"],null,null,["Kim Wilson","https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/a/ACg8ocJW4WR5h_Tp7bmgOWHBNVM5_oMTdFbDGMQpfHc8Q3sWAiyrcA=s120-c-rp-mo-br100",["https://www.google.com/maps/contrib/113996470762991177946?hl=en"],"113996470762991177946",null,2,0,null,[0,2,1],0,["2 reviews",null,null,null,null,[null,"0ahUKEwj6-ofavrOTAxWSdIQGHRKjEpQQ7LoGCBUoAA"]]]],null,"a year ago",null,null,null,null,null,null,["Google","https://www.gstatic.com/images/branding/product/1x/googleg_48dp.png",null,null,5],null,1],[[5],null,null,null,null,null,null,null,null,null,null,null,null,null,["en"],[["An absolute disgrace that I can’t speak to a nurse regarding blood results.
